fields.h1: Build an RFQ Form That Works for Buyers and Suppliers

fields.features_heading: What a Supplier Needs to Quote Without a Call
fields.features_subheading: An RFQ form defines the item so every supplier prices the same thing. These six parts cover the lines, the files, and the answers.
fields.feature_1:
A unit of measure on every line

Each line carries a part number, a quantity, and a unit picked from a list: each, foot, box, or case. A line with no unit will not submit, so 300 can only mean one thing.
fields.feature_2:
Drawings filed on the line they describe

Attach a drawing, a data sheet, or a photo to the line it belongs to. The supplier opens the RFQ and finds each file beside its part instead of in a separate email thread.
fields.feature_3:
One response sheet for every supplier

Each invited supplier gets its own link to the same fields: unit price, freight, lead time in days, and the date the quote expires. Answers arrive as rows you can sort.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders before the RFQ closes

Set a closing date and time. Two days before it, suppliers who have not answered get an email reminder, and the buyer sees which suppliers have replied and which have gone quiet.
fields.feature_5:
Each request routed to whoever prices it

Send each incoming RFQ by size, product line, or customer. Large orders can reach a senior estimator in Slack while the small ones join the inside sales queue by email.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository, then connect the form to your ERP or host it on your own servers. Keep building on the app from there.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Sends an RFQ, and Who Answers It
fields.tab_content_1:
All 12 lines arrive with a unit attached

Ilona Vasko buys for Stannard Electric, and a clinic fit-out needs 12 lines quoted by Fenmoor Electric Supply. Line 4 asked for 300 of EMT conduit with no unit. The form held it until she picked feet over 10-foot sticks. Emeka Ruthven in inside sales got the RFQ with a unit on every line.
fields.tab_content_2:
The cheapest can loses by $330 once freight is in

Pipewell Cider needs 120,000 16-ounce cans and sent one RFQ to three suppliers. Each answered the same sheet, with freight on its own line. Brightmet Containers had the lowest can at $0.131, but $1,650 in freight brought it to $17,370 delivered. Norrland Packaging came to $17,040 with freight included and won the order.
fields.tab_content_3:
Over 6 pallets, it goes to Ksenia on truckload

Ambergate Furniture asked Sorrel Line Logistics to quote 8 pallets weighing 6,400 lb from Grand Rapids to Denver, with a liftgate at delivery. Requests over 6 pallets skip the less-than-truckload (LTL) queue. This one reached Ksenia Darrow on the truckload desk by email, with the lane and the liftgate note at the top.
fields.tab_content_4:
Two suppliers split six lines, and the third hears why

Six lines went out in one janitorial RFQ from Linden Valley Health. Hedda Moorcroft gave each line to its lowest price: lines 1 to 4 to Clearbrook Sanitary for $6,240, and lines 5 and 6 to Hollis Paper Supply for $1,980. Marlpit Distributors got an email saying it ranked second on all 6 lines.

plan.angle: The live top 10 splits two ways: request-a-quote forms that suppliers put on their own sites (a WordPress plugin tutorial, two form-template sites, a freight forwarder and an equipment maker) and public-sector RFQ packets (a city's federal attachments, a state DOT matrix, a planning agency's submission form). None of them handles what makes an RFQ hard: a unit of measure on every line, the same answer fields for every supplier, freight priced so totals compare, and an award split by line. This page answers what an RFQ form is and what a standard one holds, then shows both sides using a live form: a distributor receiving a contractor's line-item RFQ, a cidery comparing can quotes on landed cost, a freight broker routing a lane request by pallet count, and a hospital buyer awarding lines to two suppliers. Proposals stay on the rfp form sibling and supplier price requests for one job stay on the quote form sibling.
tab_stories: Ilona Vasko, the buyer at Stannard Electric, sends Fenmoor Electric Supply a 12-line RFQ for a clinic fit-out, and the form stops line 4 (300 of 3/4-inch EMT conduit) until she picks feet instead of 10-foot sticks, so the RFQ reaches inside sales rep Emeka Ruthven with a unit on all 12 lines.

Pipewell Cider asks three can suppliers for 120,000 16-ounce cans, each answers the same sheet with freight as its own line, and Brightmet Containers' $0.131 can comes to $17,370 landed against Norrland Packaging's $17,040, so the lowest unit price loses by $330.

Ambergate Furniture requests a freight quote on Sorrel Line Logistics' site for 8 pallets weighing 6,400 lb from Grand Rapids to Denver with a liftgate at delivery, and because the request is over 6 pallets it goes to Ksenia Darrow on the truckload desk instead of the LTL queue.

Corin Halvorsen at Linden Valley Health awards a 6-line janitorial supply RFQ line by line: lines 1 to 4 to Clearbrook Sanitary for $6,240, lines 5 and 6 to Hollis Paper Supply for $1,980, and Marlpit Distributors gets a not-awarded email with its rank.

claims_to_source: A request for quotation is a business process in which a company or public entity requests a quote from a supplier for specific products or services
An RFQ can ask for more than the price per item, such as payment terms, quality level per item or contract length
RFQs include the item specifications so every supplier quotes on the same item
RFQs suit products and services that are as standardized as possible, which makes each supplier's quote comparable
In US federal simplified acquisitions, SF 18, Request for Quotations, is prescribed for obtaining price, cost, delivery and related information from suppliers
Under the FAR, a quotation is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract
A unit of measure is the unit in which the quantity of an item is managed, such as each, box of 12 or case of 144

domain_sources.quote: A request for quotation (RfQ) is a business process in which a company or public entity requests a quote from a supplier for the purchase of specific products or services.

domain_sources.claim: An RFQ can ask for more than the price per item, such as payment terms, quality level per item or contract length

domain_sources.quote: RfQs often include the specifications of the items/services to make sure all the suppliers are bidding on the same item/service.

domain_sources.claim: RFQs suit products and services that are as standardized as possible, which makes each supplier's quote comparable
domain_sources.quote: RfQs are best suited to products and services that are as standardized and as commoditized as possible, as this makes each supplier's quote comparable.

domain_sources.claim: In US federal simplified acquisitions, SF 18, Request for Quotations, is prescribed for obtaining price, cost, delivery and related information from suppliers
domain_sources.quote: SF 18 is prescribed for use in obtaining price, cost, delivery, and related information from suppliers

domain_sources.claim: Under the FAR, a quotation is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract
domain_sources.quote: A quotation is not an offer and, consequently, cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.

domain_sources.quote: The unit in which the quantity of an item is managed, e.g., pounds, each, box of 12, package of 20, or case of 144.
